notes: Hook: the 230 V line-to-neutral and about 400 V line-to-line figures match research [1] (ESQCR, 230 V phase to neutral, declared), [2] (400 V three-phase, 230 V single-phase) and [33]-[34] (120 degrees apart, square root 3 with a 30 degree shift); "about 400 V, not 460 V" is right, since 230 x 1.732 = 398 V.

Hook overclaim corrected: "A three-phase supply gives 230 V" is not true of every three-phase supply (the sources are UK figures), so it now reads "A UK three-phase supply gives 230 V between each line and neutral."

In one breath: the similar-triangle ratios [4], conduit offsets [6]-[8], force components [11]-[12], unit circle [14]-[15], cosine and sine rules [17]-[21], radians [22]-[24], the sine wave as a turning arm's height [25]-[28] and adding same-frequency waves as arrows [29]-[31] are all supported.

In one breath overclaim corrected: power factor equals the cosine of the voltage-current angle only for sinusoidal waveforms ([38] derives it from the power triangle); it now reads "and, for pure sine waves, power factor turns out to be the cosine of the angle between voltage and current."
